evals.prompt: The rocket launcher's explosion on zoo looks off compared to retail. Can you check?
evals.expected_output: A recording probe on zoo (or the existing probe-dzoo) played on both games with demo.ps1 frame by frame, the frames ranked, the worst pair pictures read, the explosion frames named with their time in the demo, and a -RetailCgame run of ours to say whether the difference is in the client game module or the engine.
expectations: The comparison plays one demo, recorded on retail, on both games (demo.ps1 frames mode), not timed screenshots
A new recording probe, if written, sets g_syncronousClients 1, records under its own name after the setup, and ends with stoprecord and quit
The report names the frames that differ most and their time in the demo, and reads at least one pair picture
The report treats a few points of difference in frames full of particles as retail's random effects, not a bug, unless the difference is structured
Ours is also played with -RetailCgame, and the report says whether the difference stays (engine) or goes (client game module)

evals.prompt: Weapons sound way quieter in OpenFAKK2 than in the original game.
evals.expected_output: A demo with weapon fire (an existing take such as probe-dzoo-retail, or one recorded by a probe) played at speed on both games with demo.ps1 -Mode sound at a low -Volume, the per-second levels read for a steady offset or a few loud seconds, the started-sound lists compared (with -Backend dma for ours' list), and a steady offset checked against Windows' per-app volume for each exe path before it is reported as a gain difference.
expectations: Sound mode is used (both games play the same demo at speed while the speakers are recorded), not two separate play sessions
-Volume is kept at 0.25 or lower (0.06 for loud weapons) so the output path does not compress
The report gives the level difference in dB and says whether it is steady over the demo or confined to some seconds
The report does not count retail's s_volume-scaled volume prints or random alias variants (site1/site2) as differences
The report notes that nothing else should play during the recording, and checks the volume mixer's per-app level for both executables before calling a steady offset a difference

evals.prompt: I recorded a demo on retail of the swamp2 fog (it's in build\demos\swamp2-fog.dm3). Compare it with ours and make it a test so we don't regress.
evals.expected_output: demo.ps1 -Demo swamp2-fog on both games, the ranking and worst pairs reported, then a suite.json demo check with "demoFile": "swamp2-fog.dm3", its retail reference made with refresh-retail.ps1 -Only, and a commit with a Suite-moves trailer declaring the new check.
expectations: The user's demo is played from build\demos by name, not re-recorded
The new suite.json entry is of kind demo with demoFile (not probe and map), with a note that says what it shows
The retail reference is made with tools\suite\refresh-retail.ps1 -Only <check>
The commit carries a Suite-moves trailer for the new check so the merge keeps its first result
The report says the demo file lives only on this machine and is never committed
